analysis.title: GS Flood - THE MOST CONSISTENT BUYER
key_insights: Corporates remain the most consistent buyer of US equities and their demand is accelerating, per John Flood (GS FICC & Equities).
Strong buyback growth from AI infrastructure stocks has more than offset the decline in buybacks from hyperscalers, whose capex is rising sharply.
NVDA's recent buyback authorization raised the size of its repurchase program by $150 billion to $235 billion.
GS expects US corporate buybacks of $1.7 trillion in 2027, up from $1.5 trillion this year.
Growing cash M&A will add to corporate equity demand.

Flood sees a setup for the S&P 500 to move through 8,000 in short order: corporate demand, negative investor sentiment, low net hedge fund exposure, potential supercap IPOs that could draw retail investors, and a strong earnings season starting this week.
S&P 500 gross buybacks grew 15% y/y in H1 2026, and YTD buyback authorizations of $1.1 trillion are tracking more than 20% above last year.
The GS US Equity Sentiment Indicator of investor positioning is firmly negative, and GS prime brokerage data shows light hedge fund net exposure.
Bottom-up consensus estimates show S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% y/y in Q3 2026.

GS prime brokerage data shows light hedge fund net exposure, which Flood lists as a supportive factor for an S&P 500 move above 8,000.
